headline: Aramco evacuates Dhahran HQ (first since Iran war began)
dek: Reuters (six sources): Aramco told staff to evacuate its Dhahran HQ and work remotely — first such order since the Iran war started. Saudi benchmark index TASI dropped 2.5% Thursday.
sources: Reuters via SRN https://srnnews.com/saudi-civil-aviation-says-one-killed-eight-injured-in-attack-on-king-fahd-airport/ and Economic Times https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/world-news/aramco-asks-sta
fault_line: Saudi Arabia under real threat or Ansar Allah claims exaggerated — and can US bases in the Gulf stay out of it?

sections.what_happened: Reuters (six sources): Aramco told staff to evacuate its Dhahran HQ and work remotely — first such order since the Iran war started. Saudi benchmark index TASI dropped 2.5% Thursday. Oct 23 follow-ups: Ansar Allah spokesman Yahya Saree claimed televised attacks on Aramco facilities in Yanbu and the Saudi defence ministry in Riyadh; Saudi coalition said it intercepted drones over Riyadh and Medina; Saudi Energy Ministry said 2 killed Wednesday after air defences intercepted a drone at Shaybah. Evacuation order came a day after an attack at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed 2 and injured 8 (Reuters; civil-aviation statement said 1 killed/8 injured — figures differ). US ordered non-emergency staff and families to leave Saudi Arabia (inshorts, Oct 22 20:56 -confirmed timestamp). Indian Embassy Riyadh confirmed one Indian killed, 2 injured in the Dammam airport attack, one Indian injured at Shaybah.
sections.what_verified: Indian Embassy (Riyadh) casualty confirmations; Saudi coalition interception statements; inshorts confirms US staff drawdown.
sections.what_disputed: Aramco did not comment; Saudi authorities did not confirm Yanbu/Riyadh claims; airport casualty figures differ (1 vs 2 killed). Claim that a Ansar Allah attack on Aramco HQ earlier in October caused extensive fire damage — three sources, treat as weakly sourced.
sections.why_matters: The headquarters evacuee angle: the world's biggest oil company pulls staff from Dhahran — what that signal does to oil and to Gulf security.
sections.context: Background: Aramco evacuates Dhahran HQ (first since Iran war began); TASI -2.5%; Ansar Allah-Saudi escalation widens

totw_analysis: Our read: The headquarters evacuee angle: the world's biggest oil company pulls staff from Dhahran — what that signal does to oil and to Gulf security. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Saudi Arabia under real threat or Ansar Allah claims exaggerated — and can US bases in the Gulf stay out of it?
